📈 Investment / Retirement Accounts
Cash
Anything over the pay period amount should be listed as Cash on Hand.
TFSA (Tax Free Savings Account)
Full amount is a cashable asset.
RESP (Registered Education Savings Plan)
60% of the full amount is a cashable asset. Fully exempt in Alberta.
RRSP / RSP (Registered Retirement Savings Plan)
Last 12 months' contributions are a cashable asset. Fully exempt in Alberta and Saskatchewan. RRSPs held with an insurance company (Manulife, Sun Life, Canada Life) are fully exempt.
RDSP (Registered Disability Savings Plan)
Last 12 months' contributions are a cashable asset.
RRIF (Registered Retirement Income Fund)
Fully exempt. Upon retirement, monthly withdrawals are considered income.
LIRA (Locked-In Retirement Account)
Fully exempt. Upon retirement, monthly withdrawals are considered income.
LIF (Life Income Fund)
Fully exempt. Upon retirement, monthly withdrawals are considered income.
RPP (Registered Pension Plan)
Fully exempt. Upon retirement, monthly withdrawals are considered income.
DCPP (Defined Contribution Pension Plan)
Fully exempt.
DPSP (Deferred Profit Sharing Plan)
Last 12 months' contributions are a cashable asset.
GIC (Guaranteed Investment Certificate)
Full amount is a cashable asset, unless held within an RRSP/RSP, in which case only the last 12 months' contributions are a cashable asset.
FHSA (First Home Savings Account)
Full amount is a cashable asset.
🧾 Canadian Tax Slips (T1 / T2 / T3 / T4)
T1 (Personal Return)
What it covers
Employment, self-employment, investment, rental, and other personal income.
Common income types
T4 wages, dividends, capital gains, RRSP income, rental income.
Related slips / forms
T4, T3, T5 (investment), T4A (other income), T4E (EI).
T2 (Corporate Return)
What it covers
Corporate profits, losses, and tax owing for the fiscal year.
Common income types
Business revenue less expenses equals net income for tax.
Related slips / forms
T2 Schedule 1-200; T2 Short (eligible corps); T5 if dividends paid.
T3 (Trust Return)
What it covers
Income earned by, or flowed through, a trust to beneficiaries.
Common income types
Investment income, capital gains, dividends distributed to beneficiaries.
Related slips / forms
T3 slips issued to beneficiaries; the T3 return is the trust's own filing.
T4 (Employment Slip)
What it covers
Employment income, CPP/EI deductions, tax withheld, taxable benefits.
Common income types
Salary, wages, commissions, taxable benefits, bonuses, vacation pay.
Related slips / forms
T4A for pension/other income; T4E for EI; ROE for employment record.
Tip: T4 to T1 is the most common flow. The employer issues a T4 by end of February, used to file the personal T1 by April 30. A corporation files its own T2 separately. A trust beneficiary receives a T3 slip from the trustee and includes it on their T1.
💰 Bankruptcy Refunds
Income Tax Refund
We take the refund for the year of filing, plus any prior tax returns that were not filed.
Climate Action Incentive
We take the refund for the year of filing, plus any prior tax returns that were not filed.
GST/HST
We don't take it. It's returned to the debtor if it's even issued to us. It can, however, be used to offset unpaid fees if needed.

🎯 Credit Score Factors
Payment History (35%)
R ratings and whether payments are made on time.
Utilization (30%)
How much of the credit limit has been used. Over 30% utilization is considered overutilization and brings the score down.
Credit Age (15%)
The average age across all credit accounts. Opening a new account lowers the score slightly since it lowers the average age.
Credit Diversity (10%)
More diversified credit (credit card, line of credit, student loan, utility bill, car loan, mortgage) is better for the score.
New Credit / Inquiries (10%)
Each hard inquiry lowers the score for about 1–2 months.
• Credit scores range 300–900 (normally only seen between 350–850).
• Prime lenders (banks/A lenders) typically require 670–680 for approval on a credit card, line of credit, car loan, or mortgage. Below that, only B lenders/subprime lenders at higher interest rates.
• A consumer proposal filing may drop the score by roughly 150–200 points initially (rarely below 500). About 6–8 months after filing, each on-time payment adds roughly 4–5 points a month. 1–2 prepaid credit cards plus paying off the proposal earlier than 5 years helps speed up rebuilding.
🗓️ Credit Reporting Period
Consumer Proposal
Comes off 6 years from date of filing, or 3 years after payoff, whichever comes first.
1st Bankruptcy
Comes off 6 years after the discharge date.
2nd Bankruptcy
Makes the 1st bankruptcy reappear. Both stay until 14 years after the discharge date of the 2nd bankruptcy.
Judgment
Comes off 7 years after it's posted.
Collections
Comes off 7 years after it's posted.
🛡️ Insurance Policies
Who Qualifies as a Preferred Beneficiary?
Under the historical Insurance Act definitions, preferred beneficiaries include: spouses (husband or wife), children, grandchildren, and parents (specifically "mother" in older versions).
Key Legal Protections
The primary advantage of naming a preferred beneficiary is creditor protection:
• Protection during life: any cash value within the policy is generally protected from the insured's creditors while the insured is alive, if a preferred beneficiary is named.
• Protection upon death: the insurance money is exempt from execution or seizure by the deceased's creditors, since it does not form part of the estate.
• Trust creation: in older acts, naming a preferred beneficiary automatically created a statutory trust in their favour. The insured could not revoke the designation or change the policy without the beneficiary's consent.
